Tests of model fit

Source: R/test_fit.R
test_fit.Rd

These functions test whether a model makes data like the observed data, or whether two models make the same data:

  • test_gof() compares an observed statistic with the same statistic on data simulated from a model. It is a generic, with a method for each kind of model:

    • a diffs_model, from play_diffusions(), compares an observed diffusion with the simulated diffusions;

    • a netreg, from estimate_mrqap(), simulates outcome networks from the fitted model and compares a network statistic, FUN, on each with the statistic on the observed network.

  • test_distributions() compares the data simulated from two models. It is also a generic, with a method for two diffs_model objects.

Both give a p-value from simulations, not from a distribution that the statistic is assumed to follow.

Usage

test_gof(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
test_gof(object, observed, ...)

# S3 method for class 'diff_model'
test_gof(object, observed, ...)

# S3 method for class 'diffs_model'
test_gof(object, observed, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netreg'
test_gof(object, observed, FUN, ..., times = 1000, control = list())

test_distributions(object1, object2, ...)

# Default S3 method
test_distributions(object1, object2, ...)

# S3 method for class 'diffs_model'
test_distributions(object1, object2, times = 1000, control = list(), ...)

Arguments

object

A model to simulate from: a diffs_model, from play_diffusions(), or a netreg, from estimate_mrqap(). For test_distributions(), object1 and object2 are two diffs_model objects.

...

For a netreg, additional arguments to be passed on to FUN. Other methods do not use them.

observed

The observed data. For a diffs_model, a diff_model from manynet::as_diffusion(), or a network with a diffusion record from manynet::play_diffusion(). For a netreg, the network that the model was fitted on.

FUN

For a netreg, a function of a network that returns a number or a vector of numbers, such as netrics::net_by_transitivity().

times

For a netreg, the number of outcomes to simulate. For test_distributions(), the number of permutations. A diffs_model brings its own simulations.

control

The controls of the simulations, as the result of control_mrqap() or a named list of its arguments, such as list(ncores = 4, seed = 1). A test reads ncores, strategy, and seed, and leaves the other controls alone, so that the controls of a model can be given to a test whole. ncores is generally useful only when times > 1000. A control that is not named keeps its default, or the value set with control_mrqap(..., persist = TRUE), and the result records the controls that it used as control. See control_mrqap() for each control and its default.

object1, object2

Two diffs_model objects, from play_diffusions().

Value

A network_test, which print(), tidy(), and glance() report. It holds the observed distance in testval and the reference distances in testdist.

Details

test_gof() takes the vector of statistics of each simulation, such as the number of infected nodes in each step of a diffusion, and splits the simulations into two halves. The first half gives the mean and the covariance of the statistics. The second half is the reference. The test statistic is the Mahalanobis distance from that mean, and the p-value is the share of the reference that is at least as far from the mean as the observed data: $$p = \frac{1 + \#\{d_{ref} \geq d_{obs}\}}{1 + k}$$ where \(k\) is the number of reference simulations. If the model made the observed data, the observed data and the reference are exchangeable, so this p-value is exact for any number of simulations. A reference simulation at the same distance as the observed data counts against it, so the test is conservative where distances tie. The reference does not use the simulations that estimate the mean and the covariance, so it needs no assumption that the statistics are normal.

A small ridge, a thousandth of the mean variance, is added to the diagonal of the covariance. Statistics such as an adoption curve are bounded and often constant in some steps, so their covariance is singular. With the ridge, a difference in a step where the simulations do not vary makes the distance large, and is not ignored.

test_distributions() measures the Mahalanobis distance between the mean adoption curves of the two models, with their pooled covariance and the same ridge. It then permutes which model each simulation came from, times times. As the simulations of each model are independent, this permutation test is exact.

A large distance is evidence against the model, so the p-value is Pr(X>=Obs) in print(), and p.upper in tidy().

Diffusions

The statistic of a diffusion is its curve of infected nodes, I, in each step after the seeds. A diffusion that ends early keeps its last value until the longest diffusion ends. The diffusions can come from play_diffusions(). Keep times large enough that the reference holds at least 19 simulations, or no p-value can be below 0.05.

Network regressions

The netreg method draws each simulated outcome from the fitted model with stats::simulate(), in the dyads that the model used. The other cells keep their observed values: the diagonal, the fixed ties, and the cells that the model left out. An unobserved cell is an absent tie in both the observed and the simulated networks, so they do not differ there. An undirected network is mirrored, and the simulated network takes the node attributes of the observed one.

The model needs its simple_fit, so a model fitted with less_mem = TRUE cannot be tested. A list of networks, a panel, and a cognitive social structure cannot be tested yet. Nor can a gaussian model: its draws are continuous, so every dyad of a draw would hold a tie, and the test would always reject. Fit a family whose outcomes are ties or counts.

An MRQAP models each dyad apart from the others. A statistic of the dependence between dyads, such as transitivity or reciprocity, shows what that misses.

Other packages

{RSiena} and {goldfish} export test_gof() generics with the same signature, for their own fitted models. If more than one of these packages is attached, the one attached last masks the others. Call infernet::test_gof(), RSiena::test_gof(), or goldfish::test_gof() to choose.

References

Hunter, David R., Steven M. Goodreau, and Mark S. Handcock. 2008. "Goodness of fit of social network models". Journal of the American Statistical Association 103(481): 248-258. doi:10.1198/016214507000000446

Lospinoso, Josh, and Tom A.B. Snijders. 2019. "Goodness of fit for stochastic actor-oriented models". Methodological Innovations 12(3). doi:10.1177/2059799119884282

See also

Other models: control_mrqap(), diagnose_confusion(), other_results, play_diffusions(), print.netreg_lm(), regression, specify, specify_terms, terms_mrqap, test_measures, test_parameter()

Examples

fast <- play_diffusions(ison_adolescents, transmissibility = 0.5,
                        times = 40, control = list(seed = 1))
slow <- play_diffusions(ison_adolescents, transmissibility = 0.2,
                        times = 40, control = list(seed = 1))
test_distributions(fast, slow, times = 200)
#> # Two-sample test of two sets of simulated diffusions
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   statistic null.mean null.sd p.lower p.upper signif   
#>       <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>   <chr>   <noquote>
#> 1      72.0      8.81    4.35 1       0.00498 **       
#> 
#> # Null: 200 permutations of the pooled diffusions.
#> # The p-value is p.upper: only a larger statistic counts against the null.
#> # Signif. codes: *** 0.001, ** 0.01, * 0.05, . 0.1
obs <- manynet::as_diffusion(manynet::play_diffusion(ison_adolescents,
                                                     transmissibility = 0.2))
test_gof(slow, obs)
#> # Goodness-of-fit test of the adoption curve for the simulated diffusions
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   statistic null.mean null.sd p.lower p.upper signif   
#>       <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>   <chr>   <noquote>
#> 1      16.4      26.0    31.1 0.571   0.476            
#> 
#> # Null: 40 simulations of the model; 20 estimate the mean and covariance.
#> # The p-value is p.upper: only a larger statistic counts against the null.

# Does an MRQAP make as many reciprocated ties as the observed network?
fit <- estimate_mrqap(friends ~ social + tasks, ison_algebra, times = 20,
                      control = list(family = "poisson"))
test_gof(fit, ison_algebra, net_by_reciprocity, times = 100,
         control = list(seed = 1))
#> # Goodness-of-fit test of net_by_reciprocity() for a poisson MRQAP
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   statistic null.mean null.sd p.lower p.upper signif   
#>       <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>   <chr>   <noquote>
#> 1      21.4      1.24    1.73 1       0.0196  *        
#> 
#> # Null: 100 simulations of the model; 50 estimate the mean and covariance.
#> # The p-value is p.upper: only a larger statistic counts against the null.
#> # Controls: seed = 1
#> # Signif. codes: *** 0.001, ** 0.01, * 0.05, . 0.1
